families.s: HSE COMAH notification and competent-authority submission guidance
families.t: regulation 6 notification, operator identity, establishment location, substances, quantities, activities, environment regulator, changes and submission governance
f: Operators of establishments in scope must submit a COMAH notification to the competent authority.
The notification includes operator and establishment identification and location information.
It should identify dangerous substances, categories and quantities present or likely to be present.
The establishment's activities and immediate environment should be described as required.
The competent authority combines HSE or ONR with the relevant environmental regulator.
New establishments and establishments newly brought into scope have defined notification duties.
Material changes to notified information should be reported to the competent authority.
Submission governance should ensure that information is authorised, complete, consistent and retained.
families.g: Notification quality depends on operator and establishment identity, accurate inventories and classifications, current activities and surroundings, correct competent authority, change reporting and authorised submission.

families.s: HSE explosives authorisation, licensing and certificate overview
families.t: manufacture, storage, acquisition, keeping, transfer, licences, explosives certificates, recipient competent authority and licensing authority
f: Authorisation is generally required for manufacture, storage, acquisition, keeping or transfer of explosives.
The main authorisation types are licences, explosives certificates and recipient competent authority documents.
A licence permits the holder to control specified manufacturing or storage activities.
An explosives certificate establishes fitness to acquire or keep relevant explosives.
An acquire-only certificate does not authorise overnight keeping.
A recipient competent authority document is required for covered transfers of civil explosives.
The licensing authority depends on activity, quantity, location and whether an explosives certificate is required.
Licence conditions, approved site limits and authorised activities must be followed.
families.g: Explosives authorisation depends on activity, explosive type and quantity, storage duration and location, certificate status, transfer route, licensing authority and licence conditions.

families.s: HSE explosives manufacturing and on-site-mixing guidance
families.t: manufacture definition, assembly, disassembly, repair, modification, licensing, exemptions, fireworks, on-site mixing and blasting rules
f: Most explosives manufacturing activities require a licence.
Manufacture includes making, assembling, unmaking or disassembling explosive articles or substances.
Repair, modification, reprocessing or adaptation of explosive substances can also be manufacture.
Packing, unpacking, labelling and certain testing activities are not automatically classed as manufacture.
Some firework-display preparation at the place of intended use can be exempt from a manufacturing licence.
On-site mixing at mines and quarries can be controlled through blasting rules and specifications rather than a manufacturing licence in defined cases.
Manufacture of ammonium-nitrate blasting intermediates requires the appropriate licence.
Even where a licensing exemption applies, other explosives-safety duties continue to apply.
families.g: Manufacturing status and risk depend on the process, explosive and intermediate, quantity, place, licence exemption, assembly or modification activity, blasting controls and other legal duties.

families.s: HSE explosives storage quantity, duration and effective-control guidance
families.t: licence, exceptions, net explosive mass, hazard type, temporary storage, effective control, site sharing, security and inventory
f: Explosives storage normally requires a licence from the appropriate authority.
Limited quantity and duration exceptions depend on explosive type and hazard classification.
Net explosive mass should be used when applying storage limits.
Maximum permitted quantities include explosives temporarily present at the site.
The person with effective control of the storage activity should hold the licence.
Site sharing, subletting and third-party storage require clear control and accountability.
Licence conditions and separation distances remain applicable to the authorised site.
Security controls must remain effective for the entire time explosives are kept.
families.g: Storage risk and licensing depend on explosive hazard type, net mass, duration, site layout, effective control, temporary inventory, separation, security and licence conditions.

families.s: HSE explosives fire, explosion and separation-distance safety guidance
families.t: prevention, fire spread, explosion communication, people protection, separation distance, building construction, incompatible activities, disposal and decontamination
f: Manufacturers and storers must take measures to prevent fire and explosion.
Controls should limit fire spread and communication of explosions between locations.
People should be protected from blast, fragments, heat and other effects.
Separation distances are used to control risk to neighbouring occupied buildings.
Allowed quantity may need to be reduced if development encroaches into a separation zone.
Building construction and hazard type affect the applicable separation-distance tables.
Activities that interact with explosives manufacture or storage may be controlled by licence conditions.
Disposal and decontamination of explosive-contaminated items must be planned and carried out safely.
families.g: Explosives consequence risk depends on hazard type and quantity, building construction, separation, ignition prevention, fire and explosion propagation, neighbouring occupancy, incompatible activity and emergency response.
